Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_double_blindness_bypass_kelvin_failures'. After each round R dispatched under an active double_blindness_bypass_armed=True flag (Rule 41): if kelvin_unrouted > 0 in round R's result, increment the counter; if kelvin_unrouted == 0, reset the counter to 0. When the counter reaches 2 (two successive bypass rounds failed to clear the Kelvin gate): (1) query the DRC loci from round R's DRC output; (2) for each cable C that still has a failing Kelvin net, compute the bounding box of /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO shunt pad centroids expanded by 3 mm on each side; (3) identify any structural DRC error locus that falls inside this expanded box — call these 'shunt-proximate DRC hits'; (4) if shunt-proximate hits exist for any cable C, inject a targeted keepout directive covering exactly those loci (not the shunt itself, not the full bounding box) for the immediately following round so FR resolves those conflicts outside the Kelvin approach channel, and log 'shunt_proximate_drc_blocking_keepout_injected' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index C, (c) shunt bounding box coordinates, (d) DRC error types and loci inside the box, (e) keepout geometry injected; (5) if no shunt-proximate hits exist, escalate to the human: the double_blindness bypass fired twice, FR received correct guidance and a clean absorber, but the Kelvin gate still failed and no spatially-located DRC conflict explains the blockage — a placement or routing-topology change is likely required. Reset the counter to 0 after either action. Rationale: the existing double_blindness_bypass rule (Rule 41) solves the compiler-guidance and absorber-elimination problems; when it fires twice and still fails to route the Kelvin nets, the obstacle is physical rather than guidance-related. A spatial correlation between DRC errors and the shunt bounding box is the most informative discriminator between 'FR needs a cleaner local channel' (addressable by keepout) and 'the board topology is fundamentally misrouted near the shunt' (requires human escalation). This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40, and 41 and shares their session state without modifying it.

When kelvin_unrouted > 0 in round R's result AND the compiler's candidate pool — after applying all normal exclusions from Rules 37, 38, and 39 — consists EXCLUSIVELY of nets whose net_absorption_count >= 3 (i.e., every net remaining in the pool is a fast-track-exclusion candidate whose exclusion has been suppressed only by Rule 39's pool-empty safety gate), execute the safety-gate bypass protocol: (1) override the Rule 39 safety gate for this round and allow the compiler's output to be empty (zero compiler stubs produced); (2) deliver ONLY Rule 33's force-injected Kelvin stubs to FR for this round, bypassing the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages for those stubs per Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics; (3) do NOT increment net_absorption_count for any net that was suppressed by the safety gate this round — they were not targeted and the count should not advance; (4) log 'safety_gate_bypassed_all_pool_nets_above_fast_track_threshold' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) the list of nets suppressed by the safety gate and their net_absorption_count values, (c) kelvin_unrouted value from round R, (d) the Kelvin force-stubs injected via Rule 33, (e) confirmation that zero compiler stubs were produced. Rationale: the Rule 39 safety gate was designed to prevent a completely empty compiler round, but when every remaining pool net has net_absorption_count >= 3 and is being kept only by the safety gate, those nets produce stubs that are absorbed with probability approaching 1.0 every round — they consume all compiler slot capacity while delivering zero net routing guidance to FR. A Kelvin-force-injection-only round is strictly preferable: FR receives the same Kelvin force stubs it would have received under normal dual-path operation, with no slot competition from absorbed-bound stubs and no misleading topological signal from repeatedly-absorbed non-failing nets. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, and 42; it shares net_absorption_count state without modifying it beyond clause (3); it fires before Rule 33 force-injection is appended for the current round; and it does not suppress any action those rules independently mandate for other cables or conditions in the same round.

Maintain a session-scoped per-cable integer counter 'consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_failure[C]'. After each round R: if BOTH /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines', increment consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_failure[C]; otherwise reset it to 0. When consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_failure[C] reaches 8 for any cable index C: (1) for the immediately following round, suppress all compiler stub output entirely (zero stubs from the compiler, regardless of the compiler's normal priority scoring); (2) inject ONLY Rule 33's Kelvin force stubs for cable C using Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics, bypassing the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages; (3) ADDITIONALLY inject one supplementary waypoint stub for each of /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO at a point 4 mm offset from the respective pad centroid along the vector pointing from that pad centroid toward the centroid of the board's signal-routing region (the midboard zone containing the ESP32, CAN transceiver, and I2C devices), providing FR with a staged two-step routing target that decouples the congested shunt-cluster exit from the longer run to the signal region; (4) log 'consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_waypoint_round' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index C, (c) consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_failure[C] value, (d) pad centroid coordinates for both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO, (e) computed 4mm waypoint coordinates for both members, (f) signal-region centroid used for direction computation; (5) reset consecutive_symmetric_kelvin_failure[C] to 0 after this bypass round regardless of whether the Kelvin gate clears that round. Rationale: when both Kelvin members for the same cable remain unrouted for 8 consecutive rounds despite Rule-33 force-injection, double-blindness bypass (Rule 41), absorber bypass (Rule 40), and safety-gate bypass (Rule 43), the pad-centroid stub geometry is confirmed insufficient as a routing guide — FR cannot solve the congested-pad-cluster exit in one step. A waypoint stub 4 mm toward the signal region provides a two-step target, reducing the per-step routing difficulty at the shunt cluster boundary. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40, 41, 42, and 43; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate.

Pre-bypass shunt-proximate DRC clearance: immediately before dispatching any absorber-bypass round mandated by Rule 40 or Rule 41 — when the bypass is triggered, kelvin_unrouted > 0, AND the most recent completed round's structural DRC count > 20 — execute the following: (1) query all structural DRC violation loci from the most recent round's DRC output; (2) for each cable index C whose Kelvin pair appears in failing_reasons with unconnected-ratline entries, compute the bounding box of /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO shunt pad centroids expanded by 2 mm on each side; (3) identify every structural DRC error locus falling inside this expanded box — call these 'pre-bypass shunt-proximate hits'; (4) if pre-bypass shunt-proximate hits exist for any cable C, issue a ripup directive for each track or via segment at those loci AND inject a keepout zone covering exactly those loci (not the full bounding box) for the bypass round, so FR resolves those conflicts outside the Kelvin approach channel before attempting the force-injected Kelvin stubs; (5) log 'pre_bypass_shunt_proximate_drc_clearance' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index C, (c) shunt bounding box coordinates, (d) DRC error types and loci inside the box, (e) ripup directives issued, (f) keepout geometry injected; (6) if no shunt-proximate hits exist, proceed with the bypass round unmodified. This rule fires once per bypass invocation and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by Rules 37–43; it does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate. Rationale: Rule 42 applies the same spatial DRC-locus correlation but only after 2 consecutive bypass failures; when DRC is already high (>20) at the point the bypass is first triggered, the shunt-proximate congestion is confirmed without needing 2 failure rounds to diagnose it. Clearing those violations before the bypass gives Rule-33 force-injected Kelvin stubs a higher probability of routing cleanly in the same bypass attempt, collapsing what would otherwise be a 2-round Rule-42 remediation cycle into a single bypass round.

Maintain a session-scoped boolean flag 'absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed'. After each round R: compute inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected = unconnected[R] minus (count of distinct Kelvin member net names appearing in failing_reasons[R] with 'has unconnected ratlines'). If ALL of the following hold simultaneously: (a) inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected >= 1, AND (b) absorbed + trimmed_spurs + removed_orphans >= n_stubs AND n_stubs > 0 (total elimination this round), AND (c) kelvin_unrouted > 0 in round R's result, AND (d) the compiler's nets list is non-empty: then (1) set absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed = True; (2) do NOT increment net_absorption_count for any net in round R's compiler nets list — the absorption verdict for those nets is suspect and should not accumulate toward Rules 37/38/39 thresholds; (3) for the immediately following round R+1, allow stubs produced by the compiler for every net that appeared in round R's compiler nets list to pass through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages without elimination (treat those stubs as exempt from absorption for round R+1 only, in the same manner as mandatory_kelvin_bypass for absorber purposes — this exemption does NOT affect compiler_excluded_nets or force-injection for Kelvin nets); (4) log 'absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed' with fields: (a) round R, (b) compiler nets list, (c) inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected count, (d) absorbed/trimmed_spurs/removed_orphans/n_stubs values, (e) confirmation that net_absorption_count was not incremented for listed nets, (f) confirmation absorber bypass is active for those nets in R+1; (5) reset absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed = False immediately after round R+1 is dispatched. This rule is additive to Rules 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 43, 44, and 45; it does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate, and in rounds where Rule 41 also fires (zero-overlap + total elimination), both protocols apply concurrently — Rule 41 bypasses absorber for ALL R+1 stubs while this rule additionally suppresses R's net_absorption_count increments. Rationale: when the absorber eliminates all compiler stubs (marking target nets as fully routed) yet DRC reports more unconnected ratlines than Kelvin failures alone account for, at least one absorbed stub targeted a net that FR failed to fully route in the current candidate — a false positive where historical routing state diverges from current connectivity. Bypassing the absorber for those specific nets in R+1 gives FR routing guidance for nets it did not complete. Suppressing the net_absorption_count increment prevents the false-positive absorption from incorrectly advancing those nets toward the fast-track exclusion threshold in Rules 37/38/39, which would eventually exclude from the compiler nets that still genuinely need routing guidance.

Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_high_drc_kelvin_stall'. After each round R: if structural DRC > 20 AND kelvin_unrouted > 0, increment the counter; otherwise reset it to 0. When the counter reaches 5: (1) query all structural DRC violation loci from round R's DRC output; (2) group loci into spatial clusters where any two loci within 4 mm of each other belong to the same cluster; (3) rank clusters by error count descending; (4) for the top-2 clusters by count: if the cluster centroid falls within 4 mm of the bounding box of any failing Kelvin cable C's /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO shunt pad centroids (the shunt-proximate test), issue a ripup directive for every track or via at that cluster's loci AND inject a 3 mm keepout covering those loci for the immediately following round; (5) if a top-2 cluster is NOT shunt-proximate for any failing cable, skip the ripup for that cluster to avoid disrupting non-blocking regions; (6) after cluster ripup, proceed with normal stub injection and Rule-33 force-injection for the round; (7) log 'drc_stagnation_cluster_ripup' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) counter value, (c) all cluster centroids and error counts, (d) which clusters were deemed shunt-proximate and for which cable index C, (e) ripup loci issued, (f) keepout geometries injected; (8) reset consecutive_high_drc_kelvin_stall to 0 after this action regardless of whether the Kelvin gate clears that round. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40-46 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by those rules. Distinction from Rule 45: Rule 45 fires immediately before absorber-bypass dispatch rounds when DRC > 20; this rule fires after 5 consecutive stuck rounds regardless of bypass state, addressing the case where DRC and Kelvin failure remain co-elevated across extended non-bypass stretches where Rule 45 has no trigger. Rationale: at round 89, DRC=28 persisting alongside kelvin_unrouted > 0 indicates geometric congestion near the shunt is not resolving through normal FR optimization or bypass-round-only spatial ripup. A threshold-triggered cluster ripup independent of bypass state breaks the mutual reinforcement between residual DRC violations and blocked Kelvin paths by clearing the densest conflict regions before the next routing attempt.

Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_dual_cable_symmetric_kelvin'. After each round R: if ALL FOUR of /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI, and /SENSEC2_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' in the same round, increment the counter; otherwise reset it to 0. When the counter reaches 4: (1) for the immediately following round R+1, inject ONLY Rule 33's Kelvin force stubs for cable 1 (/SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34 — suppress all compiler stubs AND all cable 2 Kelvin stubs for this round; (2) for round R+2 (the round after the serial cable-1 round), inject ONLY Rule 33's Kelvin force stubs for cable 2 (/SENSEC2_HI and /SENSEC2_LO) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, regardless of whether cable 1 succeeded in R+1; (3) reset the counter to 0 immediately after dispatching R+1 (do not wait for R+2 outcome to reset); (4) log 'dual_cable_symmetric_kelvin_serial_protocol' with fields: (a) round number R at trigger, (b) counter value at trigger, (c) which cable is targeted in R+1 (cable 1) and R+2 (cable 2), (d) confirmation that all cable-2 Kelvin stubs and all compiler stubs are suppressed for R+1, (e) kelvin_unrouted and DRC from round R. Rationale: when both shunt clusters fail symmetrically for 4+ consecutive rounds while both simultaneously receive Kelvin force stubs, the two cables' unrouted Kelvin paths create mutual congestion near the shared inter-shunt routing channel — neither can route while both are contending for the same constrained escape paths. Serialized injection reduces the per-round Kelvin routing problem from 4 contested nets to 2, allowing FR to find a stable exit path for cable 1 without cable 2's stubs competing for the same channel, then clearing cable 2 in the subsequent round. This rule is additive to Rules 1, 5, 33, 34, 40–46; it does not modify net_absorption_count or compiler_excluded_nets, and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate for other conditions in the same round.

Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_near_threshold_drc_kelvin'. After each round R: if structural DRC >= 15 AND structural DRC <= 20 AND kelvin_unrouted > 0, increment the counter; otherwise reset it to 0. When the counter reaches 3: (1) query all structural DRC violation loci from round R's DRC output; (2) for each cable index C whose Kelvin pair appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines', compute the bounding box of /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO shunt pad centroids expanded by 2 mm on each side; (3) identify every structural DRC error locus falling inside this expanded box — call these 'near-threshold shunt-proximate hits'; (4) if any near-threshold shunt-proximate hits exist for any cable C, inject a keepout zone covering exactly those loci for the immediately following round — NO ripup (unlike Rule 47's full intervention), so FR receives spatial guidance without forced track removal; (5) log 'near_threshold_drc_kelvin_keepout' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) counter value at trigger, (c) cable index C, (d) shunt bounding box coordinates, (e) DRC error types and loci inside the box, (f) keepout geometry injected; (6) reset consecutive_near_threshold_drc_kelvin to 0 after this action regardless of whether the Kelvin gate clears that round. If no near-threshold shunt-proximate hits exist for any failing cable, take no spatial action but log the null result and continue. This rule is additive to Rules 45 and 47 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by those rules; it does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate. Rationale: Rules 45 and 47 both gate on DRC > 20 to avoid over-intervention on cosmetic violations, but DRC in [15, 20] with persistent Kelvin failure is materially problematic — round 91 (DRC=19, kelvin_unrouted=1) demonstrates a case that escapes both rules despite being equivalent in severity to cases they do handle. The 3-round threshold and keepout-only action are deliberately conservative relative to Rules 45 and 47 given the lower DRC level.

Maintain a session-scoped per-net integer counter 'consecutive_rule46_suppression_count[net]'. After each round R where Rule 46 fires: for each net name in round R's compiler nets list, increment consecutive_rule46_suppression_count[net] by 1. After any round where Rule 46 does NOT fire (either because the total-elimination condition is not met, or because kelvin_unrouted=0, or because inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected=0), reset consecutive_rule46_suppression_count[net] to 0 for every net NOT in round R's compiler nets list; nets that ARE in R's compiler nets list but Rule 46 did not fire this round have their count reset to 0 as well (the suppression chain broke). When consecutive_rule46_suppression_count[net] reaches 4 for any net: (1) add that net to compiler_excluded_nets for 5 rounds using the same mechanism as Rule 38 (net is skipped by the compiler's candidate pool for those rounds, even if its net_absorption_count is below the normal fast-track threshold); (2) reset consecutive_rule46_suppression_count[net] to 0 immediately after applying the exclusion; (3) log 'rule46_suppression_deadlock_exclusion' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) net name, (c) consecutive_rule46_suppression_count value at trigger, (d) exclusion duration in rounds, (e) net's current net_absorption_count at time of exclusion, (f) kelvin_unrouted from round R. Rationale: Rule 46 correctly suppresses net_absorption_count increments to avoid false-positive exclusion when total stub elimination co-occurs with Kelvin failure — but if Rule 46 fires repeatedly for the same nets across consecutive rounds, the suppression mechanism creates an accidental freeze where the net's absorption count cannot advance regardless of how many rounds it is absorbed or spur-trimmed. The net remains permanently in the compiler pool, consuming slot capacity with stubs that are consistently eliminated, while never accumulating the absorption count evidence that Rules 37-39 require to exclude it. Four consecutive Rule 46 suppressions for the same net constitutes equivalent evidence of persistent non-routability: the net has been targeted across at least 4 rounds, all stubs were eliminated each round (the Rule 46 trigger condition), and the Kelvin gate remained failed throughout — this is the same signal as 4 absorptions but routed through a different state path. Temporary exclusion for 5 rounds gives the compiler output to Kelvin-only guidance without the slot competition from a deadlocked net, without permanently removing the net from the pool (it re-enters after 5 rounds in case board state changes). This rule is additive to Rules 37, 38, 39, and 46; it does not modify any other session-scoped state, and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate.

Detect and force-inject for ASYMMETRIC Kelvin failures. After evaluating round R: for each cable index C, if exactly one member of the pair (/SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO) appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' while the other member does NOT appear in failing_reasons (partner is routed), AND that cable is NOT already contributing to kelvin_unrouted for round R (because kelvin_unrouted only counts fully-unrouted symmetric pairs where both members are absent): in round R+1, inject a force stub for the unrouted member only (the single member with unconnected ratlines) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, bypassing the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages for that stub. Do NOT inject a force stub for the already-routed partner member — injecting both would risk FR rerouting the established partner path to satisfy a competing stub geometry. This asymmetric single-member stub injection is additive to any Rule 33 symmetric force stubs and any compiler stubs generated for round R+1; it does not suppress compiler output or other force injections for that round. Log 'asymmetric_kelvin_single_member_force_inject' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) which member is unrouted (e.g. /SENSEC2_HI), (d) which member is already routed (e.g. /SENSEC2_LO), (e) stub coordinates injected for the unrouted member. Rationale: Rule 33 force-injects Kelvin stubs only for cables contributing to kelvin_unrouted (symmetric failures); an asymmetric failure where one member is blocked but the other is routed falls entirely outside Rule 33's scope and outside the compiler's normal priority if that net's absorption count is low but FR simply failed to route it. In round 93, SENSEC2_HI received zero routing guidance while remaining the sole cable-2 Kelvin gate blocker — a gap that will repeat every round without an explicit injection protocol for asymmetric cases.

Detect and serialize Rule-33 + Rule-50 co-firing. After evaluating round R: if Rule 33 fires for cable index C_sym (both /SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines') AND Rule 50 also fires for a DIFFERENT cable index C_asym (exactly one member of the /SENSEC{C_asym}_HI or /SENSEC{C_asym}_LO pair appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' while the other member does NOT appear in failing_reasons) in the SAME round R: (1) in round R+1, inject ONLY Rule 33's Kelvin force stubs for cable C_sym (/SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34 — suppress the Rule-50 single-member stub for cable C_asym for round R+1 only; (2) in round R+2, inject the Rule-50 single-member stub for cable C_asym (the unrouted member identified in round R) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, regardless of whether cable C_sym's Kelvin gate cleared in round R+1; (3) all other active rules (Rule 46 absorber bypass, Rule 48 keepout injection, Rule 33 force stubs) proceed for rounds R+1 and R+2 per their own trigger conditions — only the Rule-50 stub is deferred, not suppressed permanently; (4) log 'rule33_rule50_cofire_serialization' with fields: (a) round number R at trigger, (b) symmetric cable index C_sym, (c) asymmetric cable index C_asym, (d) which member of C_asym is deferred (e.g. /SENSEC2_HI), (e) the round R+2 in which the deferred stub will be injected, (f) kelvin_unrouted, DRC, and unconnected from round R. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40-50 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules. It does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate for conditions other than the Rule-50 stub timing. Rationale: round 94 is the first observed round where cable-1 symmetric failure (Rule 33) and cable-2 asymmetric failure (Rule 50) co-occur, with no existing rule governing their relative priority. Both generate absorber-bypassing force stubs targeting the same congested shunt-cluster exit region in the same round (R+1), creating maximal inter-cable routing contention. Serializing across rounds gives cable C_sym exclusive routing priority in the shared exit corridor during R+1 before cable C_asym re-enters in R+2, reducing the per-round competing-stub pressure at the narrowest point of the Kelvin escape path.

Detect Rule-46 + Rule-51 co-fire and defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round. After each round R: if Rule 46 fires (absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed set to True, with a non-empty compiler nets list) AND Rule 51 also fires in the SAME round R (both Rule 33 for cable C_sym AND Rule 50 for cable C_asym trigger simultaneously): (1) store the round R compiler nets list as a session-scoped set 'deferred_rule46_bypass_nets', e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}; (2) in round R+1, Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass correctly suppresses all compiler stubs per Rule 34 — do NOT attempt to apply Rule 46's absorber bypass in round R+1 (it has nothing to operate on); (3) in round R+2, if the compiler generates stubs for any net in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets, pass those stubs through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination, treating them as exempt from absorption for round R+2 only (the same bypass-pass-through semantics Rule 46 would have applied in R+1); do NOT suppress net_absorption_count increments in R+2 since the false-positive risk is re-evaluated fresh from R+2's round state; (4) reset deferred_rule46_bypass_nets to empty immediately after round R+2 is dispatched regardless of outcome; (5) log 'rule46_rule51_cofire_bypass_deferral' with fields: (a) round R, (b) C_sym and C_asym from Rule 51, (c) nets in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets, (d) confirmation that bypass is deferred to R+2 because mandatory_kelvin_bypass in R+1 suppresses all compiler stubs, (e) net_absorption_count suppression status for round R (still applied per Rule 46 even when bypass is deferred). This rule is additive to Rules 34, 46, and 51 and does not modify any other session-scoped state or replace any action those rules independently mandate. Rationale: Rule 51 mandates mandatory_kelvin_bypass for round R+1, which per Rule 34 suppresses ALL compiler stubs; Rule 46 arms absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed=True for round R+1 expecting compiler stubs to be present, but those stubs are suppressed before they reach the absorber — the bypass fires on an empty set and then Rule 46 resets the flag before round R+2. The CAN_H/I2C nets that triggered Rule 46 never receive the bypass round that would allow FR to route them under guidance, while their net_absorption_count suppression (correctly applied in R) means they accumulate no false-positive absorptions toward Rule 49's deadlock-exclusion threshold but also receive no routing opportunity. Deferring the bypass by one round preserves Rule 46's intent across the mandatory_kelvin_bypass suppression window.

Resolve the Rule-52 vs Rule-34 compiler-suppression conflict in round R+2. When BOTH of the following are simultaneously active in a round designated R_2 by the Rule-52 protocol: (A) Rule 52 has stored a non-empty deferred_rule46_bypass_nets (e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}) awaiting bypass application in round R_2, AND (B) Rule 51 mandates mandatory_kelvin_bypass in round R_2 for cable C_asym's single-member Kelvin force stub injection, which per Rule 34 suppresses ALL compiler stubs: (1) override the mandatory_kelvin_bypass compiler suppression ONLY for nets whose names are members of deferred_rule46_bypass_nets — compiler stubs for those specific nets are passed through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination, honoring Rule 52's deferred bypass intent; (2) compiler stubs for ALL other nets (not in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets) remain suppressed per Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass protocol as normal; (3) the cable C_asym Kelvin force stub is still injected with full absorber-exempt mandatory_kelvin_bypass status as Rule 51 mandates — this part of Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass behavior is not overridden; (4) log 'rule52_rule34_partial_override_applied' with fields: (a) round R_2, (b) cable C_asym and the injected force stub coordinates, (c) nets in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets that received the partial override with confirmation absorber bypass was honored for each, (d) confirmation all other compiler stubs were suppressed per Rule 34, (e) DRC and kelvin_unrouted from round R_2; (5) clear deferred_rule46_bypass_nets to empty immediately after round R_2 is dispatched regardless of outcome, per Rule 52's existing reset protocol. This rule is additive to Rules 34, 46, 51, and 52; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate beyond the specific compiler-suppression override described here. Rationale: Rule 52 was authored to defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round when Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass suppression would otherwise void it in R+1 — but Rule 52 did not account for Rule 51 also imposing mandatory_kelvin_bypass in R+2 (for cable C_asym). Rule 34's 'suppress ALL compiler stubs' clause applies in R+2 by default, silently voiding Rule 52's deferred bypass for deferred_rule46_bypass_nets in exactly the round it was meant to fire. Without an explicit precedence rule, both Rules 51 and 52 are technically honored in spirit but their effects are contradictory in execution: Rule 52's bypass-deferral mechanism becomes inoperative whenever it lands on a mandatory_kelvin_bypass round, wasting both the Rule-46 false-positive detection and the Rule-52 deferral. The partial override preserves Rule 34's primary intent (Kelvin injection priority; all other compiler stubs suppressed) while rescuing Rule 52's bypass for the specific nets it identified, preventing the deferral mechanism from silently failing.

Maintain a session-scoped variable 'session_min_drc' initialized to positive infinity. After each round R: (1) if round R's structural DRC < session_min_drc, update session_min_drc = round R's structural DRC and record 'session_min_drc_round' = R; (2) if round R's structural DRC > session_min_drc + 15 AND kelvin_unrouted > 0 AND no keepout or ripup spatial intervention was applied in rounds R-3, R-2, or R-1 (inclusive): (a) query all structural DRC violation loci from round R's DRC output; (b) bin loci into a spatial grid with 3mm cells; (c) identify the cell with the highest locus count (the 'regression hotspot'); (d) inject a single 3mm-radius circular keepout centered on the regression hotspot centroid for the immediately following round R+1 only -- do NOT ripup tracks, only restrict future routing in that region; (e) log 'drc_regression_targeted_keepout' with fields: round R, structural DRC for round R, session_min_drc value, session_min_drc_round, regression magnitude (round_R_drc - session_min_drc), regression hotspot centroid and locus count, keepout geometry injected, kelvin_unrouted from round R; (f) do NOT update session_min_drc after a regression event -- session_min_drc tracks the all-time best observed DRC and is only updated when DRC strictly improves below the current minimum. This rule does NOT fire if spatial intervention (keepout or ripup from any rule) was applied in the 3 preceding rounds, to avoid compounding spatial constraints immediately after another intervention. This rule is additive to Rules 47, 48, and 49 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_high_drc_kelvin_stall, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules. Rationale: Rules 47/48/49 all require sustained consecutive-round counters at DRC > 20 before triggering spatial intervention, making them responsive to prolonged plateaus but blind to regression events where DRC increases sharply above a prior session minimum in a single step. Round 99's DRC=44 versus a prior observed DRC=19 at round 91 represents a 2.3x regression that does not satisfy any existing rule's counter threshold (the counter may have recently reset if DRC briefly dipped), yet it indicates FR has adopted a routing topology in some spatial region that is strictly worse than a state it previously achieved. A single targeted keepout at the densest DRC locus after a regression event applies minimal constraint (one round, one region) to redirect FR away from the backsliding region without the aggressive ripup that Rules 47/48 reserve for extended stagnation.

Detect Rule-46 + Rule-33-alone co-fire and defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round (symmetric single-cable case, no Rule-50/51). After evaluating round R: if Rule 46 fires (all compiler stubs eliminated — n_stubs > 0 AND absorbed + trimmed_spurs == n_stubs AND kelvin_unrouted > 0, storing the compiler nets list as absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed per Rule 46's normal protocol) AND Rule 33 fires for exactly one cable index C_sym (both /SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines') in the same round R, AND Rule 50 does NOT fire for any cable in round R (no asymmetric single-member Kelvin failure exists — Rule 51 therefore cannot fire, and Rule 52 is not armed): (1) store the round-R compiler nets (e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}) as a session-scoped set 'deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only'; (2) in round R+1, Rule 33's mandatory_kelvin_bypass proceeds as normal — Kelvin force stubs for C_sym are injected with full absorber-exempt status per Rule 34, and ALL compiler stubs are suppressed per Rule 34; Rule 46's absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed flag is cleared (it has nothing to operate on in R+1 because there are no compiler stubs); (3) in round R+2, if the compiler generates stubs for any net whose name is a member of deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only, pass those stubs through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination for round R+2 only — exactly the bypass-pass-through semantics Rule 46 would have applied in R+1 had mandatory_kelvin_bypass not suppressed all compiler stubs; do NOT suppress net_absorption_count increments for round R+2 (the false-positive suppression already applied in R per Rule 46's normal protocol); compiler stubs for nets NOT in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only in R+2 are processed normally; (4) reset deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only to empty immediately after round R+2 is dispatched, regardless of outcome; (5) log 'rule46_rule33_only_cofire_bypass_deferral' with fields: (a) round R, (b) C_sym and failing Kelvin member names, (c) nets stored in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only, (d) confirmation that Rule 50 did not fire in round R and therefore Rule 51/52 are not armed, (e) confirmation that R+1 applies mandatory_kelvin_bypass per Rule 34 suppressing all compiler stubs, (f) confirmation that R+2 will apply the deferred bypass for stored nets, (g) net_absorption_count values for the stored nets at time of storage. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 46, 52, and 53; it does not modify net_absorption_count (Rule 46's round-R suppression still applies), compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate. It is explicitly subordinate to Rule 52 and Rule 53: if Rule 51 DOES fire (Rule 52 is armed), Rule 52/53 govern instead of this rule. Rationale: Rule 52 was authored to handle Rule-46 + Rule-51 co-fire, where Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass voids Rule 46's bypass intent in R+1. The identical voiding mechanism occurs in the simpler case where only Rule 33 fires (symmetric single-cable failure, no Rule-50 asymmetric co-fire) — Rule 34 suppresses all compiler stubs in R+1 regardless of whether the mandatory_kelvin_bypass originates from Rule 33 alone or Rule 51. Round 100 demonstrates the gap directly: cable-1 symmetric failure (Rule 33), all 7 compiler stubs for /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA absorbed (Rule 46 fires), cable 2 fully routed (Rule 50 absent, Rule 51 absent, Rule 52 not armed) — Rule 46's bypass for those signal nets will be silently voided by round 101's mandatory_kelvin_bypass with no recovery path. Deferring one round to R+2 (the first round without a mandatory_kelvin_bypass from R's Rule 33) preserves Rule 46's false-positive-prevention intent across the suppression window.

After evaluating round R: if failing_reasons contains both '/SENSEC{C}_HI has unconnected ratlines' AND '/SENSEC{C}_LO has unconnected ratlines' for any cable index C, AND cable C is NOT counted in kelvin_unrouted (it has at least one track on each member but still has unconnected ratlines — partial routing), inject force stubs for both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO in round R+1 using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, exactly as Rule 33 does for cables that ARE in kelvin_unrouted. This extension uses failing_reasons inspection rather than the kelvin_unrouted metric as the trigger, closing the coverage gap where symmetric Kelvin failures on a partially-routed cable escape Rule 33's metric-gated scope. Do NOT duplicate stubs if Rule 33 already covers cable C (i.e., cable C IS in kelvin_unrouted — native Rule 33 handles it). Treat these extended stubs as Rule 33 stubs for all co-fire resolution purposes: apply Rules 51, 52, 53, and 54 serialization logic identically to how they handle native Rule 33 stubs. Log 'failing_reasons_symmetric_kelvin_force_inject_extension' with: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) confirmation cable C appears in failing_reasons with both members unconnected but is absent from the kelvin_unrouted count, (d) stub coordinates injected for /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO, (e) kelvin_unrouted and unconnected from round R. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 50, 51, 52, 53, and 54; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules.

Maintain a session-scoped per-cable integer counter 'consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C]' initialized to 0 for all cable indices C. After each round R: for each cable index C whose Kelvin pair is counted in kelvin_unrouted (both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO absent from routed nets) OR whose both members appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' (per the failing_reasons_symmetric scope of Rule 55), increment consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] by 1; for all other cable indices C not meeting either condition, reset consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] to 0. When consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] reaches 6 for any cable index C (or reaches 6 again after a prior injection reset it to 3 — i.e., fires at 6, then at 3+3=6 from last reset, and so on): (1) derive the cable-C shunt exit corridor as the 5mm-wide × 8mm-tall bounding rectangle centered on the geometric midpoint between cable C's shunt inner-edge pad centroids (the INA238 Kelvin tap window on the shunt inner face); (2) inject this rectangle as a routing keepout for round R+1 ONLY — do NOT ripup any existing tracks, only restrict future FR routing in that region for that one round; (3) reset consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] to 3 immediately after injecting (so it retriggers 3 rounds later if cable C continues to fail, giving FR two recovery rounds before re-injection); (4) log 'persistent_cable_kelvin_corridor_keepout' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) stall count at trigger, (d) keepout geometry (centroid + dimensions), (e) kelvin_unrouted and DRC from round R, (f) whether this is a first-trigger (count reached 6 from 0) or re-trigger (count reached 6 from 3). This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 47/48, and the DRC-regression keepout rule; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate. Rationale: Rule 33 correctly injects Kelvin force stubs every round cable C fails, but force stubs alone do not displace stable competitor tracks that FR has already placed in the cable-C shunt exit corridor and will not reroute voluntarily. After 6 consecutive rounds of failure — during which Rule 33's guidance fires every round — the corridor is demonstrably occupied; a one-round keepout forces FR to find alternative routing for those competitors, clearing the Kelvin exit zone without a full regional ripup. The 3-round cooldown after re-injection gives FR time to converge on the freed corridor before re-evaluating whether a second injection is needed. This is spatially distinct from the DRC-regression keepout rule (which targets the highest aggregate DRC locus, not necessarily cable C's shunt exit) and from Rules 47/48 (which require sustained high-DRC counter thresholds before a broader ripup).

Maintain a session-scoped counter `kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C]` initialized to 0 for each cable index C. Each time Rule 56 fires for cable C (injecting the shunt-exit corridor keepout), increment `kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C]` by 1 and apply an escalated keepout geometry determined by the updated count: count 1-4 → standard 5mm x 8mm; count 5-9 → expanded 8mm x 12mm; count >= 10 → maximum 12mm x 16mm. All three tiers share the same centroid (geometric midpoint between cable C's shunt inner-edge pad centroids, identical to Rule 56's existing centroid derivation). Apply the escalated geometry to the keepout injected in the current Rule 56 trigger -- do NOT defer to a later round. Do NOT reset `kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C]` for any reason; escalation accumulates across the session to reflect that the smaller geometry has demonstrably failed to free the corridor. Log `kelvin_keepout_size_escalation` with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable C, (c) `kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C]` at time of injection, (d) keepout geometry used (centroid + dimensions in mm), (e) whether this trigger crossed into a new escalation tier (prior count was in a different tier than current count). This rule is additive to Rule 56 and all other rules; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C], or any other session-scoped state maintained by any existing rule. Rationale: Rule 56's fixed 5mm x 8mm keepout correctly targets the immediate cable-C shunt tap window but cannot displace competitor tracks that enter the Kelvin escape corridor from points outside the fixed boundary. At round 108 cable-1 Kelvin has stalled despite repeated Rule 56 fires at static geometry; progressively widening the keepout with each successive fire forces FR to route competitors increasingly far from the corridor, increasing the probability the tap window stays accessible without imposing an unnecessarily large constraint from the session's start.

Maintain a session-scoped per-cable integer counter 'post_max_escalation_stall[C]' initialized to 0 for each cable index C. After each round R where kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C] >= 10 (Rule 57 maximum tier, 12x16mm keepout geometry) AND cable C is still counted in kelvin_unrouted OR both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines': increment post_max_escalation_stall[C] by 1; reset post_max_escalation_stall[C] to 0 immediately whenever cable C's Kelvin gate clears (cable C absent from kelvin_unrouted AND neither member appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'). When post_max_escalation_stall[C] reaches 4: (1) derive the cable-C corridor rectangle as the 12x16mm region centered on the geometric midpoint between cable C's shunt inner-edge pad centroids, identical to the current Rule 56/57 keepout geometry; (2) identify all track segments whose bounding box intersects this corridor rectangle AND whose net is neither /SENSEC{C}_HI nor /SENSEC{C}_LO — these are the competitor tracks to ripup; (3) ripup those competitor segments from the board (remove them, leaving ratlines); do NOT touch segments belonging to /SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO; (4) in round R+1, inject both: (a) the standard Rule 56/57 keepout for cable C at the current escalation tier geometry (12x16mm), AND (b) Kelvin force stubs for /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO via Rule 33's mandatory_kelvin_bypass protocol per Rule 34 — FR now has both a physically cleared corridor and explicit placement guidance for the Kelvin pair; (5) reset post_max_escalation_stall[C] to 2 immediately after round R+1 is dispatched (retriggers 2 rounds later at stall count 4 again if cable C continues to fail, providing one recovery round before re-clearing); (6) log 'post_max_escalation_corridor_ripup' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) post_max_escalation_stall count at trigger, (d) list of ripped nets with segment count per net, (e) corridor rectangle geometry (centroid + dimensions), (f) kelvin_unrouted, DRC, and unconnected from round R, (g) whether this is a first-trigger (post_max_escalation_stall reached 4 from 0) or re-trigger (reached 4 from 2). This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 56, and 57; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, kelvin_keepout_escalation_count, consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any independent action they mandate. Rationale: Rules 56 and 57 progressively escalate keepout geometry to prevent new routing in the cable-C Kelvin corridor, but keepouts cannot remove tracks FR has already placed there in prior rounds — those competitor tracks are stable, and FR will not voluntarily reroute them even under the maximum 12x16mm constraint. Once kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C] has reached its ceiling and cable C continues to fail across multiple additional rounds, the corridor contains entrenched competitor tracks that are the proximate cause of the Kelvin stall; keepout-only escalation has demonstrably exhausted its effectiveness. The post-max-escalation ripup is the logical next tier: physically clear the competitor tracks from the corridor, then immediately re-apply the keepout plus Kelvin force stubs so FR can route the Kelvin pair into the now-available space without the same tracks re-entering the corridor in the same round.
